notes: The supplied PDF contains only the instruction pages (steps 1-8); the inventory page with Element IDs was not included, so part types use LEGO design numbers (lego-<design id>, with a/b suffix variants for the antenna and round brick) from visual identification, not verified Element IDs.

The steps are small isometric pictures, so part identities, counts and exact attachment points (especially the leg/claw joints, modelled as stud connections on 1x2 handle plates) are best-effort estimates.
Each stud/anti-stud port is used by at most one join; the specific stud numbers are arbitrary labels chosen to keep joins distinct, not exact grid positions from the pictures.
The antenna is modelled with an anti-stud base (it sits on a stud) rather than a pin, so the stud/anti-stud join is compatible.
The leg plates (b16-b19, b25, b26) are modelled as hanging below the red handle plates, the side with their anti-studs; this is an approximation.

Step 8 sub-assembly (claw: dark grey handle plate, red 2x2, black 2x2, two orange plates) is attached at the left front of the body; I approximated this with a single clip joint to the base plate with no specific port.
Page 2 is a promotional page showing other models (scorpion, bird, combined spider); these are not built from this booklet and are not included.
The supplied PDF has no inventory page (page 2 only shows ads), so Element IDs are not available. Type ids use best-guess real LEGO design numbers and may not match the true Element IDs.

Piece shapes, sizes, colours and stacking positions are inferred from small step illustrations and are approximate. Step 3's extra black pieces and some white/teal/purple pieces in steps 4-6 may be missing or mis-typed.

Fixes in this version: each stud and anti-stud now has its own numbered port, so no single-use port is reused. The wheel hub is a pin-hole that fits the wheel-holder pin on the plates. The wheel uses lego-4624, a real part number (best guess for the wheel).
Black base is modelled as two 2x4 plates with wheel holders. Ids b17-b20 are skipped because the four wheels are in a repeat.
Emma's figure (hair, head, torso, skirt) is assembled in the parts box, then seated on the pink seat in step 8.
Wheels are shown as four white-and-grey wheels on the plate wheel holders; hub and tyre are treated as one piece.
The minifig's two yellow hands have no element ID in the visible pages, so they are omitted.
The inventory pages were not included. Element IDs come from step callouts, and part names are guesses from the pictures.

The printed numbers 9339 (legs) and 9551 (steering wheel) are not valid LEGO part numbers, probably because the scan is low resolution. I replaced them with the standard design IDs 73200 (minifig hips and legs assembly) and 3829c01 (steering wheel). The labels keep the printed numbers. The true element IDs need checking against the inventory page.

The booklet builds one model, the helicopter, plus a pilot minifig shown on the first page. The minifig sits in the cockpit in the final picture, so I joined its legs to a hull seat stud (b6 top.5). The exact seat position is an assumption.
Minifig joins use anti-stud/stud port kinds, because neck, hip and helmet sockets are not in the allowed kind list.

Step 5's sub-assembly joins the axle 4263624 to the tail connector 4118981, with the pin 4211807 in its hole. The pin's other end goes into the Technic brick 4233486's hole. The tail rotor sits on the free axle end. These attachments are my reading of the picture.
Colours of some parts are guessed from the images.
Step 4's sub-assembly 2 shows two 393726 pieces. I modelled them as two stacked plates on the 4233486 Technic brick.

Step 6 shows yellow round plates and black engine pods on both sides. Only one 3005744 and one 434926 are listed in callouts, so I modelled a single each. Their exact attachment points are approximated.
Stud positions can't be read from the pictures. Port names are numbered (top.1, top.2, ...) so that each stud is used by only one join.
The PDF text contained no inventory pages (no Element IDs or counts), so part types, colours and counts are inferred from the step pictures.
Exact stud positions are approximate; port numbers on joins are best guesses.

Corrected part numbers: the red round 1x1 lights now use lego-6141 (current design id for Plate, Round 1x1; 4073 is the retired number) and the trans-orange flame now uses lego-6126b (Flame / rocket exhaust element).
Other new types (lego-3070b tile 1x1, lego-93606 curved slope) are real design ids but their identification from the pictures is still an inference.
Step 2 assumed to be two 2x2 slopes; steps 11-13 black top pieces assumed to be 2x4 slopes and the windscreen.
Two 4488 wheel-holder plates assumed so that four wheels (step 14) can be attached; step 4 pictures show pegs at all four corners.

The inventory pages (Element IDs) were not in the supplied pages, so IDs are best guesses. Axle now lego-4519, wheel split into rim lego-55981 plus tyre lego-55976, beacon represented by catalogue lego-3062b in trans-orange (round 1x1 brick).
Placeholder descriptive types remain for digger arm, bucket, wheel holder, exhaust bracket and minifig pieces, since their real Element IDs cannot be read from the supplied pages.
The lego-2540 handle port is a clip-type port, so the arm's matching port was changed to a bar (clip/bar is compatible).
Pictures are small; exact stud positions are not resolved, so many joined edges have null ports.
Step 3-4 piece identities are approximated as two wedge plates, two black 1x4 plates and two red 1x1 tail-light plates; hood approximated as lego-3037; seat as a blue 1x2 plate.
Minifig has hat, head, torso (with arms/hands) and legs.
